sub_question: SQ1: Standards & indices — how do raw concentrations map to user-facing respiratory-risk categories?
summary: The US EPA Air Quality Index (AQI) is the standard translation layer from raw µg/m³ to six color-coded risk categories (Good 0-50 → Hazardous 301+). AQI=100 for any pollutant equals its short-term NAAQS. The 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups' band (101-150, Orange) is the pivotal trigger for respiratory-patient advice; the reported AQI = the single worst pollutant's sub-index.
key_insight: For a respiratory-focused agent the actionable threshold is LOWER than for the public: the AQI is intentionally built so that 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups' (101-150) fires FIRST for people with asthma/COPD. So the agent should escalate advice at AQI ~100+ (and per-pollutant), not wait for the 'Unhealthy' (151+) public threshold. The device reports the MAX sub-index across pollutants, so it must compute each pollutant's sub-index and surface which pollutant is driving the number.

aqi_categories.meaning: sensitive groups (incl. respiratory) may have effects; general public less likely — KEY respiratory trigger
general public may have effects; sensitive groups more serious
health alert: increased risk for everyone

detail.anchor_rule: AQI value of 100 for a pollutant = its short-term National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS); <=100 generally satisfactory.
detail.reporting_rule: Overall AQI = the highest individual pollutant sub-index; agent should expose the driving pollutant, not just the composite number.
index_variants_to_compare_later: EU EAQI (1-6 scale, uses WHO-aligned bands)
WHO AQG (limit values, not an index)

notes: AirNow/EPA is authoritative for the US AQI; category ranges + descriptions quoted verbatim from the page table. Exact per-pollutant breakpoint concentrations (the piecewise-linear sub-index formula) not yet captured — defer to a later cycle only if the schema (SQ5) needs them.
